critical.issue: Old admin credentials 'admin@uonogamesapk.com / Admin@12345' still return 200 with a valid JWT. The credential rotation only added the new admin — the previous admin user document from iteration 1 was never removed or invalidated. Requirement said 'old ones should fail'. Fix: in seed(), delete or disable users whose email != current ADMIN_EMAIL AND role == 'admin', OR run a one-time migration to purge the stale admin.

minor.issue: to_object_id raises HTTPException(400) on malformed id — good. But calling with a valid-format but non-existent 24-char hex hits ObjectId conversion inside update/delete/get code paths that don't wrap DB errors. Currently returns 404 in practice via find_one — acceptable, but no explicit try/except around the ObjectId path in delete_faq/update_faq.

rca_of_the_issue: OLD credentials still work RCA: server.py seed() at lines 450-464 only checks the CURRENT ADMIN_EMAIL. When ADMIN_EMAIL was changed from 'admin@uonogamesapk.com' to 'arfuu9@gmail.com', the previous admin document (with its bcrypt hash of 'Admin@12345') was left untouched in db.users. login() at line 189 looks up the user by whatever email is posted, so both admins remain valid. Reproduction: `curl -X POST $REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL/api/auth/login -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"email":"admin@uonogamesapk.com","password":"Admin@12345"}'` returns 200 with a JWT. Mitigation (one-liner in seed): `await db.users.delete_many({'role': 'admin', 'email': {'$ne': admin_email}})` — or a targeted db.users.delete_one({'email':'admin@uonogamesapk.com'}).
